# Results

## The article is already a strong noun lever

With the intervention off, inserting `an` versus `a` moves the
full-vocabulary noun distribution by TV \(0.937\) \([0.891,0.975]\) on
the 20 held-out prompts. A transformers-only baseline, with no sparse
intervention, gives TV \(0.940\) \([0.893,0.976]\) on the same 20 prompts
and TV \(0.975\) \([0.964,0.983]\) on 95 released `an`-target occupations;
the top-1 noun changes on every prompt in both splits. Any sparse handle
that flips the article therefore has a large, generic continuation
channel available before leftover internal control is considered.

## Free generation looks coordinated; the six cells split it

Amplifying S1 at \(5\times\) moves every held-out prompt to `an` and
changes the greedy noun on 19/20 prompts (@tbl-packaging). Concrete twins
include `a pilot`\(\rightarrow\)`an aviator` and
`a lawyer`\(\rightarrow\)`an attorney`. Matched random features and S3 do
not produce this switch. Those free-generation rates show that S1 is a
specific handle on legal article--noun completions. They do not identify
the transmission route.

| Condition | \(N\) | \(\Delta\) art.\ logit favors `an` | Noun token preserved | Class shift | Wrapper-like | Package-like | Twin match |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| S1 \(5\times\) | 20 | 1.00 | 0.05 | 0.95 | 0.00 | 0.95 | 0.35 |
| S1 control | 20 | 0.70 | 1.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| S3 \(5\times\) | 20 | 0.70 | 0.95 | 0.05 | 0.00 | 0.05 | 0.00 |

: Free-generation metrics (held-out occupations). Wrapper-like = generated
article moves and noun token stays; package-like = legal article--class
switch. These rates do not identify leftover noun control.
{#tbl-packaging}

The six-cell split does. S1 at \(5\times\) selects `an` on 20/20 prompts.
Inserting that treated article with the intervention **off** reproduces
the S1-on top-1 noun on 20/20 prompts. Across all 20 prompts, total TV is
\(0.893\), token-substitution TV is \(0.891\), and matched-prefix leftover
TV is \(0.028\) \([0.021,0.035]\) (@tbl-mediation; @fig-mediation A).
Cosine of \(E_M\) with \(E_T\) is \(0.949\) \([0.849,1.000]\); cosine of
\(E_R\) with \(E_T\) is \(0.124\) \([-0.112,0.355]\). Reconstruction
\(\|E_T-(E_M+E_R)\|_1\) is numerically zero (implementation check).
Frozen attention in the original S1 factorial yields the same qualitative
split.

| Attention | Total TV | Token-substitution TV | Leftover TV under treated article | Treated-token top-1 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Recomputed (primary) | 0.893 | 0.891 | 0.028 [0.021, 0.035] | 1.00 |
| Frozen (ablation) | 0.893 | 0.891 | 0.026 [0.020, 0.033] | 1.00 |

: S1 \(5\times\) six-cell split on all 20 held-out prompts. Intervals are
prompt-bootstrap 95\% intervals.
{#tbl-mediation}

The remaining forced cell supplies the complementary rescue. Restoring the
baseline article while leaving S1 active restores the baseline top noun on
20/20 prompts; the on/off distributional difference under that restored
article is TV \(0.030\) \([0.025,0.036]\). Thus the treated article is
sufficient to phenocopy the treated top noun, and the baseline article is
sufficient to rescue the baseline top noun despite the upstream intervention.

The leftover is not exactly zero, and it is not confined to the treated
article. On seven listed twins, target-minus-source \(\Delta\Delta\) is
\(0.018\) \([-0.071,0.107]\) under inserted `a` and \(0.089\)
\([0.027,0.152]\) under inserted `an`. Individual `an` leftovers are
pilot\(\to\)aviator \(+0.125\), lawyer\(\to\)attorney \(+0.062\),
physicist\(\to\)astronomer \(+0.062\), photographer\(\to\)artist
\(-0.062\), psychologist\(\to\)anthropologist \(+0.125\),
geologist\(\to\)archaeologist \(+0.250\), farmer\(\to\)agriculturist
\(+0.062\). Free-generation target/source contrast on the same twins is
about \(11.6\) logits; treated-article insertion alone contributes about
\(11.6\) logits (post-hoc descriptive).

![S1 vector split against the generic article lever, and six-cell leftovers across handles and S1 dose.](manuscript/figures/fig_mediation_decomposition.png){#fig-mediation width=94%}

## Dose: the large total effect is gain-gated; the leftover is not

At \(1.5\times\), S1 writes `an` on only \(2/20\) prompts and total TV
collapses to \(0.065\). The leftover under inserted `an` is already
present: TV \(0.015\) and twin \(\Delta\Delta\) \(0.098\)
\([0.027,0.161]\). At \(3\times\), free `an` rises to \(0.90\), total TV
to \(0.802\), and token substitution still dominates (cosine of \(E_M\)
with \(E_T\) remains high). The dramatic free-generation rewrite is
therefore gated by whether the gain is large enough to engage the
article boundary of TV \(0.937\). The small leftover under `an` is not
created only by \(5\times\).

## Prompt-aligned boundaries expose discrete causal amplification

We binary-search each prompt's S1 gain until its article margin is bracketed
within \(0.0039\) gain units. Nineteen of 20 prompts cross between gains 1 and
5. Across them, the cross-boundary noun change is TV \(0.938\)
\([0.889,0.978]\); token substitution alone is TV \(0.939\)
\([0.889,0.977]\), with cosine \(0.9998\) \([0.9996,0.9999]\) to the total.
Over the same interval, each fixed-article distribution moves only \(0.014\)
TV. Greedy decoding therefore converts a tiny continuous change into a nearly
maximal downstream jump: a discrete causal amplification, not a comparably
large persistent latent rewrite.

## Family comparison: only S1 produces a large article-flipping rewrite

@tbl-family compares \(5\times\) handles; @fig-mediation B also shows S1 dose.
Only S1 produces a large free-generation article+noun switch, and that switch
remains token-substitution dominated. S3, the attribution-selected
content-ish set, does not move nouns (total TV \(0.025\); noun-changed
rate \(0\)). The selected S3 set therefore does not supply matched-prefix
noun control; this set-level null does not establish a general failure of
future-token attribution. S4 never writes `an`. S2 never writes `an` either;
greedy strings often derail (`called a \ldots`, `not a biologist`), so its raw
noun-change rate is a parse artifact rather than a coordinated rewrite.
Forensic reanalysis nevertheless prevents dismissing S2 as mere noise: only
7/20 S2-on free continuations are legal article--noun completions, but under
fixed `an` all seven pre-specified twins move toward their target, with mean
\(\Delta\Delta=+0.830\) \([0.545,1.125]\). The forced-`an` top noun changes on
only 1/20 prompts. We therefore classify S2 as **target-aligned subthreshold
private influence mixed with free-generation disruption**, not as a clean
persistence-dominant intervention. The S1 leftover under `an` (\(+0.089\))
overlaps the random control (\(+0.071\) \([0.027,0.134]\)). We therefore do
not claim a specific noun plan from the S1 residual.

Individual and leave-one-out runs localize S2's two phenotypes. L5/F383 alone
keeps all 20 free continuations legal while retaining fixed-`an` TV \(0.096\)
\([0.075,0.118]\) and twin \(\Delta\Delta=0.768\)
\([0.500,1.009]\), positive on 7/7 twins. Removing L5/F383 collapses the
fixed-`an` TV to \(0.020\) and the twin effect to \(0.205\). Conversely,
removing L11/F12690 makes all 20 free continuations invalid while leaving the
fixed-token signal intact. Thus a single sparse feature carries most of the
fixed-token class-aligned influence, whereas derailment is a nonlinear
coalition phenotype. Only four other layer-5 features met the frozen
activation-matching rule; their mean TV is \(0.013\) and twin effect \(0.036\),
but this small eligible pool gives minimum empirical \(p=0.20\) and is not a
definitive null distribution.

| Handle | Free an | Noun changed | Treated top-1 | Total TV | Token-subst. TV | Leftover TV (an) | Twin \(\Delta\Delta\) a | Twin \(\Delta\Delta\) an |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| S1 \(5\times\) | 1.00 | 0.95 | 1.00 | 0.893 | 0.891 | 0.028 | 0.018 | 0.089 |
| S2 \(5\times\) | 0.00 | 0.70 | 0.86 | 0.109 | 0.000 | 0.101 | 0.018 | 0.830 |
| S3 \(5\times\) | 0.05 | 0.00 | 1.00 | 0.025 | 0.000 | 0.021 | 0.062 | 0.018 |
| S4 \(5\times\) | 0.00 | 0.35 | 1.00 | 0.028 | 0.000 | 0.021 | \(-0.107\) | 0.080 |
| Random \(5\times\) | 0.05 | 0.05 | 1.00 | 0.019 | 0.000 | 0.020 | 0.000 | 0.071 |

: Six-cell family sweep at \(5\times\) on the same 20 held-out prompts. S2/S4 noun-changed rates often reflect illegal greedy strings. S2's vector split is defined only on prompts whose free articles are a or an.
{#tbl-family}

Appendices E--G establish cross-token reachability, stack sensitivity, and
estimand polarity: S1 changes later CLT activations; a layer-12 full-residual
reference moves target logits; and known article-only versus persistent
generators yield leftover TV \(0\) versus \(0.667\), respectively.

## Target-specific influence survives from the pre-article position

The stronger pre-article reference directly tests the missing
\(t\rightarrow t+2\) route. Layer 12 is selected on four development pairs.
On 12 disjoint same-article-class pairs, patching the target-cued full residual
at \(P\) while inserting the shared native article `a` shifts the
target-minus-source contrast by \(+1.339\) logits
\([1.021,1.677]\), compared with \(+0.215\) \([0.081,0.357]\) for ten
matched-norm random directions averaged within pair (@fig-public-private A).
The mean full-vocabulary TV is \(0.073\) \([0.054,0.095]\). The target does not
become top-1 on any held-out pair, so this is target-specific private-state
capacity, not persistence-dominant behavioral control.

The same patch remains target-aligned under inserted `an`:
\(\Delta\Delta=+0.703\) \([0.526,0.875]\), versus \(+0.120\)
\([0.029,0.215]\) for matched random directions. Crossing public article with
private patch yields a public effect of \(+0.609\) logits
\([0.224,0.984]\) with the private patch off, \(-0.026\)
\([-0.385,0.359]\) with it on, and interaction
\(\Gamma=-0.635\) \([-0.839,-0.448]\) (@fig-public-private B). Public and
private causes are therefore separately manipulable and non-additive in this
target-constructed reference. This does not yet show that a natural sparse
feature allocates the same lexical state between the registers.

![A pre-article target residual moves held-out nouns under a fixed visible article; crossing article identity with the patch reveals an interaction. Error bars are pair-bootstrap 95\% intervals.](manuscript/figures/fig_pre_article_public_private.png){#fig-public-private width=84%}
